Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — NordicHealth is trying to close the legal review for our pilot and we have a couple of high-priority asks around EU-only processing and SCCs following Schrems II. High-level questions below:

- Can Redwood commit that production inference data (inputs/prompts, outputs, KV caches) will be processed and stored only within EU territories when we select EU-only routing?
- Is the control plane metadata (billing, usage metrics, account identifiers) ever routed or stored in the US for hosted customers?
- Do you support customer-managed KMS keys for the EU region (we prefer CMEK in our subscription)?
- What logging/audit evidence can you provide to demonstrate deletion (for both automated retention and manual on-request deletes)?
- Can you share a data flow diagram and a redline-ready SCCs template (we may want to present to our DPO and counsel).

Goal: short call to resolve open items this week and then share SCC redline.

Thanks,
Jurgen Schmidt
Head of Security — NordicHealth
jurgen.schmidt@nordichealth.com

Hi Jurgen — thanks, we can cover all of this. High-level answers first, then suggested next steps.

- EU-only processing: For our Dedicated and Private deployments we can guarantee that inference workloads, token storage, and KV caches remain inside a specified EU region (we run regional clusters in DE, NL, and FR). For our Hosted API the default is region-aware routing; when you request EU-only routing we pin inference to EU clusters, but note there are two caveats: (1) the global control plane (account metadata/usage metadata) is hosted on a private control plane option — if you need full control-plane residency we recommend the Private deployment; and (2) cross-region fallbacks are configurable (we can set strict no-fallback policy).
- Control plane: by default, hosted control plane services are in our EU cluster for customers who select EU-only; however, historical usage metadata may be replicated for analytics — we can provide contract language to restrict replication and set retention.
- KMS/CMEK: we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private, and we have limited CMEK availability for Hosted via our enterprise add-on.
- Deletion & evidence: we provide API endpoints for deletion + a deletion audit log. Standard retention defaults are configurable; we can provide exportable audit logs and a certificate of deletion for manual erasures.

Next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Rishi (security/compliance) with a detailed data-flow and SCCs fallback matrix — he has the technical matrix you asked for.
2) We’ll share a redline-ready SCCs doc and a short action plan (MA plan) for NordicHealth to review.
3) Suggest a 30-minute call on Feb 16 to walk both technical and legal teams.

Attestation: We can commit contractually to EU processing for production inference in Dedicated/Private deployments and to strict routing controls for Hosted with contractual restrictions; we will provide supporting audit evidence.

Best,

Hi Jurgen / Olga — adding the technical specifics and what we can include in the SCCs supplementary measures. See bullets below and attached artifacts.

- Regional routing: Requests are routed by policy at the edge; when EU-only routing is enabled we enforce locality via regional load balancers and ingress policies. We maintain strong affinity to EU clusters; failover to non-EU regions only happens if/when explicitly allowed in routing policy (we can set "no failover").
- Data at rest: All inference stores (prompt store, response cache, KV cache) are encrypted at rest using AES-256. For Dedicated/Private we offer CMEK (customer-managed KMS) so keys never leave your control. For Hosted with enterprise add-on we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account SOLID keys.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups in Dedicated are region-scoped; we can disable cross-region snapshots for EU-only commitments. For Hosted customers we can offer contractual limits on replication.
- Access controls & personnel: EU-only deployments can be configured to limit access to employees who are EU-based and have role-based approvals; we also support customer-managed IP allowlists and zero-trust connections.
- Logs & deletion: We expose an API that returns deletion receipts and a machine-readable audit of deletion events (timestamp, object id, initiator). Default application logs are retained for 30 days; retention is configurable down to 0 days.
- Supplementary measures: We can include pseudonymization of identifiers, encryption-in-use mitigations (VM isolation, strict attribution), and contractual audit rights. The suggested SCCs redline will include language mapping to these measures.

Olga / Rishi — thanks, that's helpful. Couple follow-ups before the call:

- Retention: You mentioned default app logs at 30 days and configurable down to 0. Can you confirm whether input prompts (raw prompt text) are retained anywhere beyond the inference window unless explicitly stored by the customer? We need assurance that there isn't a hidden debug-store that keeps prompt bodies beyond retention policy.
- Deletion certification: Can Redwood provide a signed deletion certificate (or machine-verifiable audit proof) for on-request deletions? Our DPO prefers an automated receipt that shows object ids and timestamps.
- SCC redline: please include explicit language that forbids cross-border replication of prompt data and restricts subprocessors to a named list with EU locations; we will provide procurement-preferred clause language but want to see Redwood's initial position.

Also, please attach the data-flow PNG and the SCC matrix to the HubSpot ticket so our procurement team sees it.

Best,
Jurgen

Answers to your follow-ups:
- Prompt retention: By default, raw prompt text is kept only in the short-lived inference buffer (seconds) unless a customer opts into prompt logging or explicitly persists prompts via our storage API. For customers who enable prompt persistence, retention follows the configured retention policy and can be deleted on request; we do not keep a hidden debug store that retains prompt bodies beyond configured retention. We can provide a redacted example audit showing a deletion receipt in machine-readable format.
- Deletion certification: Yes — we provide an automated deletion receipt (JSON) with object id, deletion timestamp (UTC), and actor. For enterprise contracts we can add a signed attestation on request.
- SCC redline & subprocessors: Rishi has included our recommended supplementary measures; the SCC redline in the attached PDF maps to that language. We will produce a formal subprocessors addendum listing EU-located subprocessors only for your EU-only commitment.
